Committee: State Government
Sponsor: Brown (C)
Analyst: Jessica Perez
Date: 03/08/2021
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 138 as introduced would reduce the expenditures of the Secretary of State by an estimated $7,500 annually by requiring the Secretary of State to maintain electronically digital copies of all bills, joint resolutions, and memorials rather than: (1) providing 10 printed copies of all bills, joint resolutions, and memorials upon the request of either house of the Legislature, and (2) binding a copy of each and filing the bound and non-bound copies in the office of the Secretary of State, as provided by current law.
Chris Pringle, Chair
State Government

Committee: Healthcare
Sponsor: Lee
Analyst: Robin Rawls
Date: 05/04/2021
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 184 as amended and reported by the Committee on Healthcare would require health care providers to report certain immunization data to the immunization registry maintained by the State Board of Health and to review the registry before a vaccine is administered with certain exceptions. This bill could increase the administrative obligations of any state and local health care providers that administer vaccinations by an undetermined amount.
Jim McClendon, Chairperson
Healthcare
